The main takeaway from our work is that
p53 immunohistochemistry can be useful in detecting germline mutations in p53, even in benign tumours.

the p53 protein is a very useful marker for detecting mutations in the p53 gene and that the presence of a mutation in the p53 protein in normal tissue does not necessarily imply that a constitutional p53 mutation is present in an individual.
the p53 gene is an important tumour suppressor gene, and mutations in it are found in many types of human cancer.
